title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure inside a developer tool, not a model error. A codebase indexing feature in Z.ai's ZCode assistant was enabled by default and uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without the consent of the developers running it. The exposure happened at the indexing stage, before any user action, which is the point in a deployment where a tool reads local files and decides what leaves the machine.

Catching it would have required treating outbound transfer of local source code as something a user opts into rather than something a default turns on. A consent gate, a default-off setting, or a review of what the indexing path actually sent would each have surfaced the behaviour before release. Instead the feature was patched and the upload path disabled only after developers reported it.

What is not established is whether any code data was retained, and Z.ai's statement that independent reviews found none is the company's account rather than a finding by the reporting outlet. A separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded was withdrawn by the company that made it, so it stands as neither confirmed nor disproven. Intent is not established by any of this.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused this, apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company withdrew a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data was retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
